entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Nikolai Ivanovich Feshin, better known in English as Nicolai Fechin, was a Russian and American painter known for his portraits and works featuring Native Americans. After graduating with the highest marks from the Imperial Academy of Arts and traveling in Europe under a Prix de Rome, he returned to his native Kazan, where he taught and painted. He exhibited his first work in the United States in 1910 in an international exhibition in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. After immigrating with his family to New York in 1923 and working there for a few years, Fechin developed tuberculosis and moved West for a drier climate.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Fechin's works featuring Native Americans helped to shift American art towards greater representation of indigenous peoples, contributing to a more nuanced understanding of Native American experiences. His legacy can be seen in the work of later artists who followed in his footsteps.
